explanation_full:
The incremental feature analysis table demonstrates how the performance metrics (R² and MSE) change as features are added sequentially. For the KNN model, the best performance (highest R² and lowest MSE) was observed when 9 features were used (VFA -> Butyrate -> Acetate -> VSS -> Propionate -> Ethanol -> COD-O -> pH -> ORP_Low), achieving an R² of 0.8301 and an MSE of 0.0119. This suggests that the inclusion of the 'ORP_Low' feature, given the preceding 8 features, significantly boosted the model's predictive power. 

Comparing the final benchmark results (11 features), KNN maintained strong performance with an R² of 0.8172 and an MSE of 0.0128. Across all models, KNN consistently outperformed the others, including RF (R²=0.7756, MSE=0.0157) and XGBoost (R²=0.7495, MSE=0.0176). 

In summary, the analysis suggests that KNN is the best model, and the feature set including the first 9 features provides optimal performance, although the final 11-feature set maintains high performance. The overall best model performance is confirmed by the summary text, which reports KNN with R² = 0.81717 and MSE = 0.012810.
